speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Colon Cancer to the Neck.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of colon cancer (colectomy at age 43) presenting with a painless, progressively enlarging swelling on the nape of his neck for two months, accompanied by diabetes and hypertension. Given the history of malignancy and the specific characteristics of the swelling, metastatic disease is highly suspected.

REQUEST TEST: CT Neck with contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Neck_Slice.
